title: Pareto-Conditioned Diffusion Models for Offline Multi-Objective Optimization
claim: Recasting the problem as conditional generation lets a single trained model map target objectives directly to designs, with no surrogate or separate optimizer.
layout: 2 dashed panels, left-to-right; training then sampling, block arrows between stages
description: Two rounded dashed-border panels sit side by side. The left panel is blue and labeled 'Static Multi-Objective Dataset'. It shows a yellow database cylinder marked D, with molecule and DNA icons and a candlestick-style chart icon beside it. A blue arrow leads down to a second 'Reweighted' dataset cylinder with a balance-scale icon. A second blue arrow labeled 'Train' leads to a boxed 'Pareto-Conditioned Diffusion Model' with a faint neural-network graphic behind the text. The right panel is orange and shows the sampling stage. A Gaussian curve feeds down into the model box through an arrow labeled 'Noise'. A blue 'Target Objectives' box with a chart icon feeds the model through an arrow labeled 'Condition'. An arrow labeled 'Sample' leads down to a 3D 'Designs' block flanked by molecule and DNA icons. Block arrows carry the flow, and color separates training from inference.
caption: Overview of the PCD framework, which reframes offline MOO as a conditional sampling problem. Training: A conditional diffusion model is trained on a static dataset, using a novel reweighting strategy to emphasize high-quality solutions near the Pareto front. Sampling: At inference, the model directly generates novel designs conditioned on target objectives. This end-to-end approach sidesteps the need for the explicit surrogate models and separate optimizers required by prior methods.
abstract: Multi-objective optimization (MOO) arises in many real-world applications where trade-offs between competing objectives must be carefully balanced. In the offline setting, where only a static dataset is available, the main challenge is generalizing beyond observed data. We introduce Pareto-Conditioned Diffusion (PCD), a novel framework that formulates offline MOO as a conditional sampling problem. By conditioning directly on desired trade-offs, PCD avoids the need for explicit surrogate models. To effectively explore the Pareto front, PCD employs a reweighting strategy that focuses on high-performing samples and a reference-direction mechanism to guide sampling towards novel, promising regions beyond the training data. Experiments on standard offline MOO benchmarks show that PCD achieves highly competitive performance and, importantly, demonstrates greater consistency across diverse tasks than existing offline MOO approaches.
